title: Reconcile Staging One-Click tunnel lifecycle authority

phases.objective: Keep the operator-safe default local-only, make tunnel ownership transitions publish one canonical runtime authority, and make Staging database access-repair handoff exact-plan verifiable before any local execution.

e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The no-argument launcher remains local-only; explicit public modes require the Staging Activation Gateway before topology mutation, use a bounded transition lease, and publish tunnel_mode/tunnel_started atomically to the exact-commit runtime state after success.
steps: Launch the operator CMD without a tunnel argument and resolve disabled as the safe default.
Reject a public tunnel mode before topology mutation when Activation Gateway authority is absent.
Enter a bounded deployment lease before delegating the selected tunnel transition to the dual-mode core.
On successful transition, atomically publish tunnel_mode and tunnel_started while preserving the exact runtime commit, then remove the lease.
On failed transition, retain a short transition-failed lease so the Health Monitor does not misclassify an in-progress or failed handoff as healthy steady-state authority.
assertions: The CMD and smart launcher default to disabled local-only mode.
Explicit windows_service or docker_sidecar CMD selection includes EnableActivationGateway.
Public modes without EnableActivationGateway fail before Invoke-Core can mutate topology.
Successful transitions atomically update canonical autopilot-state.json tunnel_mode and tunnel_started with exact-commit readback.
Failed transitions leave only bounded Staging lifecycle evidence; no Production, provider, Cloudflare DNS, schema, migration, or Production database mutation is authorized.

e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: A Staging database.access_repair dry-run returns a concrete request JSON and non-placeholder local command; the local verifier rebuilds the repository-owned plan and rejects any plan_sha256 mismatch before delegating to the existing Host Breakglass runner.
steps: Build the Staging database.access_repair plan against the exact deployment SHA and staging_local_role_env target source.
Return local_execution_required with a concrete verified request envelope containing the canonical plan_sha256 and a deterministic request_sha256.
Persist the returned JSON locally under the deterministic request filename and invoke the returned Windows/Docker local command.
Verify request shape and digest, rebuild the repository-owned Host Breakglass plan from the request, and require exact plan_sha256 equality before invoking the existing local runner.
Run the repository dry-run without database mutation; a later apply_grants remains separately ticketed, typed-confirmed, server-reserved, and same-cycle-readback governed.
assertions: The handoff no longer returns <verified-request.json> as an unusable placeholder.
The request is restricted to staging_local_windows_docker + database.repair + database.access_repair + staging_local_role_env.
Tampering with expected_sha or any request field invalidates request_sha256 before the legacy runner, Docker mutation path, or database path is reached.
The local verifier requires the rebuilt plan_sha256 to equal the server-returned canonical plan_sha256.
Production authority remains false and the handoff itself performs no database, provider, Cloudflare, schema, migration, or Production mutation.

phases.objective: Preserve shared source compatibility without authorizing Production execution.
blockers: Production remains outside this repair and requires its separate governed promotion lifecycle.
